conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. The consensus looks beatable in USD because the rand closed August stronger (ZAR16.10/USD) than the consensus implies, and South African vehicle demand is strong. Against that, management pre-warned on 16 July that new-customer distribution would slow over the next three quarters, and net adds are the line this name has traded on: -12% in Oct 2025 on decelerating adds, +11.2% in Jul 2026 on a record 142k. The CEO also sold steadily until the August blackout. The findings net to 0.0. p_up 51 carries only the FX-translation lean, so expected_move is near zero while abs_move stays at the name's real earnings-reaction scale of about 8.5%.
bar: Q2 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026). Consensus EPS is $0.57 with a $0.60 whisper and revenue $97.72M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/KARO, fetched 2026-10-19). MarketBeat has EPS $0.589 and revenue $98.81M (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-karooooo-karo-set-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-06/, 2026-10-06). The two roughly agree. At the 31 Aug 2026 rate of about ZAR16.10/USD (https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/ZAR-USD-2026) that is about ZAR9.2-9.5 EPS against Q1's ZAR9.53 and Q2 FY26's ZAR8.28, and ZAR1,573-1,591m revenue against Q1's roughly ZAR1,560m. Company guide, reaffirmed 15 Jul 2026: FY27 EPS ZAR38.50-40.00, Cartrack subscription revenue ZAR5.7-6.0bn, GM 70-72%, OPM 27-30% (https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/KARO-Q1FY2027-SENS-20260716.pdf). There is no subscriber guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest was 214,139 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 66,254 on 09-15 (+223%) and the highest in 23 settlements. That is 2.34 days to cover on about 92k ADV and about 0.7% of the 30.9m shares outstanding. Free float is far smaller because the CEO holds about 17.6m directly, so the short is perhaps 1.5-2% of float. Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/karo/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-19. This is not a crowded short, but it built sharply into the quarter. There is no listed options market, so no skew. Run-up is -6.66% over 20 days and -0.96% over 5 days, 11% below the 52-week high, partly the rand weakening in October (ZAR/USD 0.0617 Sept average to 0.0607 on 19 Oct).

findings.finding: The USD consensus is low against Q1's run-rate once translated at the quarter-end rand. $0.57-0.589 EPS and $97.7-98.8M revenue at ZAR16.10 (31 Aug) is ZAR9.2-9.5 EPS, below Q1's 9.53, and only +0.8-2.0% QoQ revenue. The rand strengthened from 16.21 at end-May to 16.10 at end-Aug, and Q2 FY26 subscription revenue grew about 3.6% QoQ. A typical ~3% QoQ ZAR revenue gain prints about $100M, roughly 1.5-2.5% above the bar. EPS near ZAR9.6 prints about $0.60, matching the whisper. Q1 likewise beat ($0.59 vs $0.51). Netted: Q2 FY26 EPS dipped seasonally QoQ (8.55 to 8.28), so the EPS beat is less certain than the revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS line from confirmed releases: May 2026 Q4 FY26 EPS $0.44 vs $0.51 consensus, stock -6.07%. Jul 2026 Q1 FY27 $0.59 vs $0.51 with record adds, +11.23%. Both also turned on subscribers, so EPS is not the line by itself.
findings.why_not_priced: US aggregators set the USD consensus and seldom re-translate it at the period-end rand. If the market had priced a mechanical USD beat, the stock would not be 11% off its high and down 6.7% over 20 days into the print. This is FX arithmetic, not a fundamental surprise, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Company ZAR bases (Q1 revenue and EPS, Q2 FY26 EPS 8.28) are from https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/KARO-Q1FY2027-SENS-20260716.pdf and https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/KARO-HY26-Q2-SENS-20251015.pdf. The consensus is from two aggregators. The FX series is independent of both.

findings.finding: On the 16 Jul 2026 Q1 call, management said Cartrack would lean more on cross-selling to the existing base than on new-customer distribution over the next three quarters. It said distribution growth is planned to be slower this year, with onboarding and training as the constraint, and declined to give subscriber guidance. So Q2 net adds likely step down from the record 142,472. The prior-year Q2 was 70,740, and Q3/Q4 FY26 were 111,478 and about 93,755. The stock is priced off a record headline adds number it just paid +11% for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net adds are the line this stock trades on. Oct 2025: net adds slowed to 70,740 from 89,168 and the stock fell about 12% intraday despite a maintained outlook (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/15/karooooo-earnings-cartrack-shines/). Jul 2026: a record 142,472 (+70%) and +11.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was said on a webinar, not in the release, and the press release headline was 'record net adds, accelerating growth'. If the market expected a step-down, the post-Q1 +11% would have faded more than it has (stock about $61 vs about $65 after the print, partly FX). Pre-warning means a moderate decline is partly expected, which keeps the size modest.
findings.independence: Prior-year and sequential net-add history is from company releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828102/000121390026005643/ea027330101ex99-1_karooooo.htm and the Q1 SENS PDF). The boilerplate finding below bounds the downside on the same line from a different document.

findings.finding: The company's own 'About' boilerplate moved from 'more than 2.8 million active subscribers' (6-K, 8 Jul 2026, Q1-end 2,804,694) to 'over 2.9 million' (6-K, 5 Oct 2026). That means at least about 95k net adds between 1 Jun and early October. The boilerplate tracks a current count: Oct 2025 said 'more than 2,475,000' against a Q2 FY26 end of 2,456,989, and May 2026 said 'more than 2,700,000' against a Q4 end of 2,662,222. This rules out a collapse in adds but is consistent with anything from about 70k to 150k in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same net-adds line as above: -12% on a deceleration (Oct 2025), +11.2% on a record (Jul 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates boilerplate subscriber counts. It is only a lower bound, so it removes the left tail of the adds outcome rather than setting a point, and it is sized small.
findings.independence: Comparison boilerplates: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828102/000121390026076218/ea029739301ex99-1.htm (2026-07-08), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828102/000121390026051953/ea028919601ex99-1.htm (2026-05-05), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828102/000121390025096281/ea026036901ex99-1_karooo.htm (2025-10-06). These are all company documents and they shade the net-adds finding above rather than contradict it.

findings.finding: South African new-vehicle sales stayed strong through Cartrack's Q2. NAAMSA had June 2026 as the highest June in 19 years and August domestic sales of 57,898 (+11.4% YoY, 23rd straight month of growth), with September +12.7%. South Africa drove Q1's record (SA net adds +92%) and insurers commonly require tracking on financed vehicles.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no direct history. SA-driven net adds coincided with the +11.2% Jul 2026 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series, so it is largely priced. It is a proxy that the company has not confirmed for Q2, and the company is steering away from new-customer distribution, which caps the transmission.
findings.independence: Proxy. June record: https://www.timeslive.co.za/motoring/2026-07-01-south-africas-new-vehicle-sales-hit-highest-june-total-in-19-years/. Q1 SA +92% in company release (Q1 SENS PDF).

findings.finding: Powerfleet (owner of MiX Telematics, a direct South African fleet-telematics competitor) said on 10 Aug 2026 that it is reallocating resources to its SA National Treasury contract and forgoing portions of projected non-strategic South African revenue. That points to slightly lower competitive intensity for Cartrack's SA fleet business.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer's call that KARO coverage does not read through. It is a proxy whose effect on one quarter is tiny.

findings.finding: CEO and 57% holder Isaias Calisto sold steadily in the open market, not under a 10b5-1 plan, from 27 Jul to 26 Aug 2026 at about $63-64. Holdings fell from about 17.92m to 17,631,026 shares (about 287k shares, about $18M), roughly 13k shares/day against about 77-92k ADV. Twelve Form 4s stop on 27 Aug, consistent with a quarter-end blackout. The trading window reopens after this release, so the same supply can return during the reaction window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The selling began 12 days after the +11.2% Q1 reaction and coincides with the stock drifting from about $65 to about $61.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s are public, but whether the sales resume right after the print is not. If the market had priced the overhang it would show in the 20-day drawdown, which it partly does. It is sized small because the blackout may extend past 20 Oct.
findings.independence: First filing in the series: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828102/000121390026082607/ownership.xml (2026-07-29, 47,949 shares at $63.44-64.19, 10b5-1 flag 0).

findings.finding: Short interest tripled into quarter-end. It was 214,139 shares at 30 Sep vs 66,254 at 15 Sep, the highest of 23 settlements, at 2.34 days to cover, after falling from 148k in mid-July. Someone positioned against the print, though the level is small against the float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved pattern for this name. At 2.3 days to cover on a thin float, the squeeze risk is real on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: FINRA data is public but read by few people on a 77k-share/day name. The sign is ambiguous (informed bear vs squeeze fuel), hence the small size and wide band.

findings.finding: Samsara, the largest listed fleet-telematics peer, reported on 3 Sep 2026 for the quarter to 1 Aug: revenue +30%, net new ARR +28% YoY, and a raised FY guide. That shows robust fleet-telematics demand during Cartrack's Q2, though in a different geography and customer tier.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print and therefore public. Its transmission to an SA consumer- and SME-heavy base is weak, which is why it is sized near zero.

rejected_candidates.detail: The 6-K matcher counted AGM, dividend and date notices (EDGAR 6-K list: 2026-07-02 and 07-23 AGM, 07-28 AGM results, 07-08 date notice). The base rate was rebuilt from confirmed releases: Oct 2025 about -12%, May 2026 -6.07%, Jul 2026 +11.23%.

rejected_candidates.detail: Same FX series as finding 1. The guide is in ZAR and assumes current rates, and the October move is already in the ADS price (part of the -6.66% 20-day run-up).

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The -6.7% 20-day run-up is partly the rand and partly CEO-sale supply, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the balanced read. The findings net to zero, and only abs_move carries information here.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (lands inside what the company guided): the net-adds finding moved from -1.5 to -1.2, because management pre-warned slower distribution on the Q1 call. It was not set to zero because there is no subscriber guide and this line has moved the stock 11-12% each way.

Rule 7 (short interest before a negative): checked. At 2.3 days to cover and about 0.7% of shares it is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk. The CEO-selling finding moved from -0.5 to -0.4 because the blackout end date is uncertain.
Rule 5 (proxy small): the Samsara peer finding moved from +0.2 to +0.1. NAAMSA and Powerfleet were left as small proxies.

Lesson on contaminated FPI history: the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed releases, and abs_move was raised from 8.0 to 8.5 and p_up from 49 to 51 now that the findings net to zero apart from the FX-translation lean.
Rule 6 (bar): two aggregators roughly agree ($0.57/$0.589, $97.7M/$98.8M), so no cap was applied.
